title: Chase 'Part of Our Site Isn't Working Right Now' Error: 6 Solutions [2026]
content:
Encountering the generic banner **"We're sorry, part of our site isn't working right now. Please try again later"** is one of the most common and ambiguous errors on Chase.com. 

This error typically appears when attempting to view credit card statements, load transaction histories, or initiate wire transfers. It usually signals that an internal Chase microservice is temporarily unresponsive while the primary authentication gateway remains online.

## What Does "Part of Our Site Isn't Working Right Now" Mean?

**This error indicates an API microservice failure within Chase’s distributed cloud architecture.** While your main login handshake succeeded, the specific sub-system responsible for statements, rewards, or transfer ledgers failed to respond within the expected timeout threshold.

| Diagnostic Detail | Information |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Bank** | JPMorgan Chase Bank |
| **Error Message** | "Part of our site isn't working right now" |
| **Common Trigger Areas** | Statements & Documents, Credit Card Rewards, Transfers |
| **Average Resolution Time** | 3 - 10 Minutes |

> 🔴 **Status Update:** This error frequently spikes during scheduled database maintenance windows, typically occurring between 1:00 AM and 4:00 AM Eastern Time on weekends.

## 6 Step-by-Step Fixes for This Error

Follow these troubleshooting steps to bypass the stalled session:

### 1. Hard Refresh Your Browser (Bypass Stale Assets)
Standard page refreshes reload cached scripts from your hard drive. A hard refresh forces your browser to re-download Chase's live code:
* **Windows ([Chrome](/guides/chase-online-banking-not-working-on-chrome)/Edge/Firefox):** Press **Ctrl + F5** or **Ctrl + Shift + R**.
* **Mac (Chrome/Safari):** Press **Cmd + Shift + R** or hold Shift while clicking the browser reload button.

### 2. Log Out Completely and Clear Session Cookies
Simply closing the browser tab leaves orphaned authentication tokens active on Chase's servers:
1. Click the **Log Out** button in the top-right corner of the Chase portal.
2. Close all browser tabs.
3. Open a new window, navigate to `chase.com`, and sign back in.
*A fresh token often reconnects you to a healthy, balanced server node.*


> 💡 **Related Chase Bank Solution:** Encountering related issues? Check our verified fix for [Chase Error Code 99 Login Failed: Complete Fix Guide](/guides/chase-error-code-99-login-failed).


### 3. Switch to the Chase Mobile App
Because Chase partitions desktop web traffic and native mobile app traffic into separate API clusters:
1. Open the **Chase Mobile App** on your smartphone.
2. Navigate to the exact feature (e.g., Transfer, Statements, Bill Pay) that failed on desktop.
*In over 80% of microservice outages, the mobile cluster continues functioning smoothly.*

### 4. Bypass via Account Quick Links
If the primary dashboard fails to render your accounts list:
1. In your browser's address bar, navigate directly to: `https://secure.chase.com/web/auth/dashboard#/dashboard/overview`
2. Alternatively, try accessing the transfer portal directly: `https://secure.chase.com/web/auth/dashboard#/dashboard/payTransfer/payBills/overview`
*Direct URL routing often circumvents broken homepage widgets.*

### 5. Disable Browser Extensions and VPNs
Third-party browser extensions (especially translation tools, password autofills, and VPN proxy tunnels) can corrupt the JSON payload response:
* Open an **Incognito / Private Window**.
* Turn off any active VPN connections.
* Try loading the page again without third-party network filters.

### 6. Change DNS Provider to Cloudflare or Google
If your ISP's recursive DNS resolvers are caching stale routing tables for Chase's Content Delivery Network (Akamai):
1. On Windows or Mac, open your **Network Settings**.
2. Set your custom IPv4 DNS to **1.1.1.1** (Cloudflare) or **8.8.8.8** (Google).
3. Flush your DNS resolver cache in terminal via `ipconfig /flushdns` (Windows) or `sudo dscacheutil -flushcache` (Mac).

## How to Check Official Chase Server Status

When internal microservices fail on a national scale, thousands of users experience this exact message simultaneously.
* **Downdetector:** Check the Chase page on Downdetector for immediate outage spikes.
* **Chase Customer Support on X:** Check [@ChaseSupport](https://twitter.com/ChaseSupport) for official incident notifications.

> ⚠️ **Security Warning:** Beware of sponsored Google search ads claiming to be "Chase Urgent Help Lines." Always call the customer service phone number printed on the back of your physical card.

## Prevention Tips

To minimize encountering stalled Chase web sessions:
* **Avoid Banking During Maintenance Windows:** Avoid major transfers during early Sunday morning hours when maintenance is scheduled.
* **Keep Sessions Short:** Log out promptly after completing banking tasks rather than letting sessions time out in background tabs.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

**Does this error mean my bank account has been hacked or restricted?**
**No.** "Part of our site isn't working" is strictly a technical website server error. It has no bearing on your account standing, credit score, or security status.

**Can I still withdraw cash from an ATM during this error?**
**Yes.** Physical ATMs connect directly to core mainframe banking switches that are independent of consumer web interfaces. Your debit card and PIN will function normally at any ATM.

**How long does this Chase outage typically last?**
**Most microservice hiccups are resolved by Chase cloud load-balancers within 15 to 30 minutes.** If related to scheduled maintenance, full service typically restores by 6:00 AM EST.

**What should I do if an urgent bill payment is due today?**
**If you cannot submit a payment online, call Chase Automated Telephone Banking at 1-800-935-9935.** The automated phone system operates independently of web servers and can process bill payments 24/7.
